turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good afternoon, thanks for calling Acme Life, this is Chloé speaking. Just so you know, this call is recorded for quality and training purposes. How can I help you today?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hi. I saw your ad online for term life with no medical exam. I want to know what the catch is before anyone tries to sell me anything.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Fair enough, I'm happy to walk you through it. Before I go into any details or a quote, can I confirm your full name and date of birth, please?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Olivia Roy. March 14th, 1986.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thank you, Olivia. I have that as Olivia Roy, born March 14th, 1986. Is that right?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: That's right.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Great. So, Acme Term Life is a term policy. You pick a 10- or 20-year term, and your premium is fixed for the whole term, so it won't go up partway through. There's no medical exam. Instead, acceptance is based on a few health questions.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Okay. And what happens at the end of the term? Do I get anything back?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No. This policy has no cash value, so there's no payout if the term ends and you're still around. It's pure protection: it pays out if you pass away during the term.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Right. At least you're straight about that. How much coverage are we talking?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Coverage goes from fifty thousand up to seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars. Honestly, for someone your age, I'd go with five hundred thousand on a 20-year term. That's what most people in your bracket end up choosing, and it's a really solid amount.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Five hundred thousand? That seems like a lot. You don't even know what I do or what I owe.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: It's a nice round number that covers most things people worry about, like a mortgage or family expenses. Five hundred on a 20-year term is the sweet spot. Let me get you a price on that.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Fine, but just a price. I'm not committing to anything.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Of course. I just need to ask you a few health questions first. In the past five years, have you been diagnosed with or treated for heart disease, cancer, or stroke?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Have you used any tobacco or nicotine products in the last twelve months?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, I quit about four years ago.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good for you. Are you currently taking any prescription medication for diabetes or high blood pressure?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No. I'm pretty healthy. I'm on my feet all day, I'm an electrician. Self-employed.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Perfect. Based on those answers, you qualify. For five hundred thousand dollars of coverage over 20 years, your premium would be ninety-two dollars a month, fixed for the full 20 years.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Ninety-two a month. Hmm. Okay, I want to think about it, maybe compare a couple of other companies. Can you email me the quote?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: I could, but to be honest, this rate is only available while we're on this call. If you hang up and call back, it gets re-quoted and it probably won't be ninety-two. People who wait usually end up paying more.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Really? That sounds like a sales line. Why would the price change in a day?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: It's just how the pricing works on our end. The ninety-two is locked in today if we do it now. Thinking it over doesn't really change much, you already know what it is and what it costs.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I don't love being rushed. What if I sign up and then change my mind next week?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: You have a 30-day free-look period. If you cancel within 30 days, you get a full refund. So there's no downside to locking it in now.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Thirty days, full refund, no strings?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's right, a full refund within the 30 days.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Okay. I'd rather have something in place than nothing. My guys are on job sites all the time and you never know. Let's do it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Great. Before I complete this, let me summarise. This is Acme Term Life, five hundred thousand dollars of coverage on a 20-year term. Your premium is ninety-two dollars a month, fixed for the full term. There's no cash value, and you have a 30-day free-look period with a full refund. Do you want to go ahead with this policy?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, I want to go ahead.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thank you, Olivia. I'll take your payment details now, and your policy documents will be emailed to you within a couple of business days.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Fine. Let's get it done.
